l: Hannah Topping, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Hannah admits Georgiana and Sir Tristram to the police-station and secretly tells them that the Dean is in the cell. She has arranged an escape involving a whistle and Nick the fire-brigade horse, but discovers that Noah has taken Kitty instead.

l: Noah Topping, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Noah acts as the local constable at the police-station and initially proposes that the missing Dean committed suicide. He brings the Dean out of the cell in handcuffs, claims charges against him, and takes him toward Durnstone, apparently using Kitty in the cart instead of Old Nick.

l: Dr. Jedd, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Augustin Jedd, the Dean of St. Marvells, is reported missing but is found by Noah in the police-station cell. He says he was administering a simple remedy for chills to a suffering horse, and Noah takes him away in handcuffs despite Georgiana and Sir Tristram's attempt to secure his release.

l: St. Marvells, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: St. Marvells is the place where Noah and Hannah have recently arrived, and Augustin Jedd is its Dean.

l: Durnstone, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Durnstone is where the Bench sits and where Noah intends to take the Dean. Noah also says that the Dean's case can be reported there.

l: the police station, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: The police-station receives Georgiana and Sir Tristram when they come to report the Dean's disappearance. The Dean is being held in its cell, and Noah operates there as the constable.

l: the Deanery, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: The Deanery is Augustin Jedd's residence and is associated with the stables where he was found. The Dean urges that the drawing-room fire and his warm bath and clean linen be prepared there because he expects to return.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Dandy Dick was dosed the previous night, and Augustin Jedd was found administering something to a suffering beast connected with that incident. The analysis of what was administered has not yet come back from the chemist.

l: old Nick, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Old Nick is the fire-brigade horse that Hannah expects to help bring the Dean back to the Deanery. Noah leaves Old Nick at home instead of using him in the cart.

l: Kitty, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Kitty is put in Noah's cart while Old Nick is left at home. Hannah realizes that this substitution prevents the Dean's planned escape.

l: the Dean's disappearance, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Georgiana and Sir Tristram report that Augustin Jedd disappeared after retiring to rest and could not be found in the morning. The disappearance is complicated by the discovery that he is being held in the police-station cell.

l: the Dean's alleged suicide, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Noah theorizes that the missing Dean's disappearance is an ordinary case of suicide. Georgiana and Sir Tristram reject the idea, and the Dean is subsequently found alive in the cell.

l: the arrest of the Dean, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Augustin Jedd has been arrested after being found trespassing in the stables at the Deanery. Noah brings him from the cell in handcuffs and takes him toward Durnstone.

l: the Dean's treatment of Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: The Dean says he was administering a simple remedy for chills to a suffering beast. Georgiana says the analysis has not yet returned from the chemist, so the treatment's nature is not yet established.

l: the alleged trespassing and attempted larceny, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: The Dean faces a charge arising from being found in the Deanery stables, while Hannah warns that another, more serious charge hangs over him. Noah also says that he is charging the Dean with alienating his wife's affections.

l: the Dean's whistle, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: The Dean has Hannah's whistle. Hannah intends for the whistle, together with Nick the fire-brigade horse, to help bring him safely back to the Deanery.

l: Noah's cart, Dandy Dick, [_HANNAH unlocks the door, and admits GEORGIANA and SIR TRISTRAM, both dressed f
s: Noah's cart is outside the police-station and is intended to carry the Dean to Durnstone. Hannah discovers that Noah has put Kitty in the cart and left Old Nick at home.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Georgiana and Sir Tristram rescue the Dean after he is pursued and forcibly brought home from the Hill, while Major Tarver and Mr. Darbey secure Salome's and Sheba's acceptances. The Dean discovers that Salome and Sheba attended a masked ball at Durnstone and won fifty pounds at the Races, while Georgiana won fifteen hundred pounds over the Handicap. The analysis of the bolus reports sixteen grains of strychnine, but Blore confesses that he added it while trying to remove Dandy Dick from the race and mistakenly wagered the Dean's money on Bonny Betsy. The Dean admits that he instructed Blore to back Dandy Dick for the Restoration Fund, and the unit ends with Salome and Sheba confronting him about his deception and proposed marriages.

l: Salome, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Salome accepts Major Tarver after Darbey presents his supposed medical need for marriage. She and Sheba are revealed to have attended the masked ball at Durnstone, won fifty pounds at the Races, and incurred part of the £40 19s costume bill. She later confronts the Dean about his deception and announces that she and Sheba intend to begin life afresh after receiving marriage proposals.

l: Sheba, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Sheba accepts Mr. Darbey after briefly asking for time to consider his proposal. She and Salome are revealed to have attended the masked ball at Durnstone, won fifty pounds at the Races, and incurred the £40 19s costume bill. She later confronts the Dean about his deception and proposed marriage.

l: Augustin Jedd, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Augustin Jedd, the Dean, is rescued by Georgiana and Sir Tristram after being forcibly taken home from the Hill. He admits that he instructed Blore to back Dandy Dick for the Restoration Fund, is horrified to learn that the bolus contained strychnine, and finally faces his daughters' discovery that he deceived them about his absence.

l: Major Tarver, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Major Tarver arrives at the Deanery in an extremely weak condition, supported by Mr. Darbey. He claims that rejection by Salome will destroy his health, produces a doctor's certificate, and is accepted by Salome.

l: Mr. Darbey, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Mr. Darbey brings the weak Major Tarver to Salome and Sheba and claims that the Major must propose to recover his health. He proposes to Sheba, who accepts him after asking for a brief period to ponder the question.

l: Georgiana, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Georgiana helps Sir Tristram rescue the Dean from the Hill by rallying race-course associates to their aid. She reveals that she won fifteen hundred pounds over the Handicap and later agrees to marry Sir Tristram. She also helps expose Blore's addition of strychnine to the bolus.

l: Sir Tristram, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Sir Tristram assists Georgiana in rescuing the Dean and carries him back to the Deanery. He reveals that he owns one-half of Dandy Dick, denounces the Dean after learning that the bolus contained strychnine, and proposes to Georgiana, who accepts him.

l: Blore, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Blore confesses that he added strychnine to the bolus because he wanted Bonny Betsy to win instead of Dandy Dick. He admits that he placed the Dean's fifty-pound offering on Bonny Betsy rather than Dandy Dick, and the Dean keeps him in service in exchange for silence.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Dandy Dick is the horse that won the Races in a common canter. The Dean had instructed Blore to back Dandy Dick for the Restoration Fund, and Sir Tristram and Georgiana are revealed to own one-half each of the horse.

l: Bonny Betsy, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Bonny Betsy finished behind Dandy Dick and was described as walking in with the policeman. Blore had intended to remove Dandy Dick from the race so Bonny Betsy could win, and mistakenly placed the Dean's wager on her.

l: the Deanery, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The Deanery is the setting in which the Dean is brought home, his daughters' attendance at the masked ball is exposed, and the bolus is discussed. Blore threatens to reveal what happened there but remains in its service after the Dean demands his silence.

l: St. Marvells Spring Meeting, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The Races are attended by Georgiana, Salome, and Sheba, with Georgiana winning fifteen hundred pounds over the Handicap and the girls winning fifty pounds. Dandy Dick wins, while Bonny Betsy loses.

l: Fancy Dress Masked Ball at Durnstone, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The masked ball at Durnstone took place the night before the Dean returned home. Salome and Sheba attended it in costumes representing a lady of the French Revolution and a flower-girl of an unknown epoch.

l: the Restoration Fund, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The Restoration Fund is the stated purpose for which the Dean instructed Blore to back Dandy Dick. The Dean expected the wager to provide five hundred pounds towards the Spire.

l: the Bolus, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The bolus was presented as a simple remedy for a chill and was intended by the Dean to affect the race outcome. Blore secretly introduced a foreign element into it, and its analysis reported sixteen grains of strychnine.

l: the analysis, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The analysis of the bolus is brought to the Deanery by the chemist. It reports that the bolus contains sixteen grains of strychnine, prompting Sir Tristram and Georgiana to denounce the Dean before Blore confesses.

l: strychnine, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Strychnine was added to the bolus by Blore in an attempt to get Dandy Dick out of the race. The analysis states that the bolus contained sixteen grains.

l: the account for the fancy dresses, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The £40 19s costume bill is a debt to Lewis Isaacs, Costumier to the Queen, for costumes used at the masked ball at Durnstone. The Dean discovers it and orders Salome and Sheba to account for it, but they say they can pay it with their winnings.

l: the Restoration Fund money, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The Restoration Fund money consists of the fifty pounds the Dean gave Blore to wager on Dandy Dick. Blore instead placed it on Bonny Betsy, which lost.

l: the thousand-pound wager, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The race wager was made with the Dean's fifty pounds and was intended for Dandy Dick on behalf of the Restoration Fund. Blore mistakenly placed it on Bonny Betsy after altering the bolus.

l: the Dean's deception, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: The Dean's deception includes hiding his absence and his involvement in the race wager from his family. Salome and Sheba discover that he has stooped to deception, while he also learns that they concealed their attendance at the masked ball and their gambling winnings.

l: the proposed marriages, Dandy Dick, _The second scene is the Morning Room at the Deanery again.
s: Major Tarver proposes to Salome and Mr. Darbey proposes to Sheba; both proposals are accepted. Sir Tristram also proposes to Georgiana, and she agrees to marry him.

l: Dandy Dick, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Noah Topping rushes into the Deanery with Hannah, accusing the Dean of being the unknown man who escaped his custody after allegedly alienating Hannah's affections. The Dean establishes that he is not the culprit and invites Noah and Hannah to dine in the kitchen. Georgiana tells the Dean that his own deception has caused his family influence and dignity to collapse, while promising that George Tidd may lend money for the poor old Spire. The company agrees that laughter at the Dean's expense is acceptable when it is directed at folly rather than virtue and comes from friends.

l: Noah Topping, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Noah Topping rushes into the Deanery with Hannah, claiming that an unknown lover of his newly made wife was rescued from his lawful custody. He mistakenly identifies the Dean as the man he captured, but Hatcham reveals that the actual man was short and thin. The Dean invites Noah and Hannah to stay for a hot dinner with ale, and Noah urges Hannah to thank him.

l: Hannah Topping, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Hannah Evans, now Mrs. Topping and the bride of the constable, clings to Noah and tries to lead him away from the Deanery. She apologizes for Noah's ignorance and asks the Dean to forgive him. She thanks the Dean after he invites them to dine in his kitchen.

l: Dr. Jedd, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Dr. Jedd is identified as the Dean of St. Marvells, not as the unknown man whom Noah captured. He responds mildly to Noah's mistake, withdraws any charge against the unknown person found on his premises, and shows kindness by inviting Noah and Hannah to dinner.

l: Georgiana, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Georgiana tells the Dean that his family influence has gone and his dignity has been crushed by deception. She says that George Tidd will lend him a thousand for the poor, innocent old Spire, provided he admits there is no harm in laughing at a Sporting Dean. She explains that the Dean himself has been riding the horse called Deception hardest.

l: Sir Tristram, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Sir Tristram helps establish that the Dean is not the man secured in the stable by going out and bringing in Hatcham. He later tells the Dean that there is no harm in laughter, whether directed by those who laugh or at those who are laughed at.

l: Augustin Jedd, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: The unknown man was rescued from Noah Topping's custody after Noah's face was held down in the mud, and Noah says he was an unknown lover who had alienated Hannah's affections. Noah traces him to the Deanery, but Hatcham states that the man secured in the stable was short and thin and was not the Dean.

l: the Deanery, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: The Deanery is the place to which Noah traces the unknown man. The Deanery's kitchen is offered as the location for Noah and Hannah to stay and dine.

l: Deception, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Deception is described by the Dean as having frosted the genial summer of the Deanery with the winter of Deceit. Georgiana says that once a person begins to use deception, it takes control and becomes difficult to stop.

l: the horse called Deception, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Georgiana compares Deception to a horse that takes the bit between its teeth once it is driven with the whip. She says that the Dean has been riding this horse hardest.

l: laughter at the Dean's expense, Dandy Dick, Directly they have disappeared, NOAH TOPPING, looking dishevelled, rushes in at
s: Georgiana asks the Dean to accept laughter at the expense of a Sporting Dean. Sir Tristram says laughter is harmless, and Georgiana qualifies it as proper when it mocks folly rather than virtue and comes from friends.

l: Gallegher and Other Stories, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Gallegher, an office-boy at the Philadelphia Press, identifies a gloved man traveling to Torresdale as Stephen S. Hade, the fugitive suspected of murdering Richard F. Burrbank and stealing $200,000. He learns that the man, calling himself Mr. Carleton, is staying at the Eagle Inn and may attend the big fight there that night. Gallegher telegraphs Detective Hefflefinger and reports the discovery to Michael E. Dwyer, who plans to have Hade arrested quietly and transported to New York. The Press's managing editor had discharged Gallegher for playing truant, but Dwyer proposes that the paper reinstate him if the arrest succeeds.

l: Gallegher, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Gallegher is a young office-boy at the Press with extensive street knowledge and a strong interest in crime. He recognizes a man with a possibly artificial finger as Stephen S. Hade, follows him from the Kensington railroad station to Torresdale and the Eagle Inn, and telegraphs Detective Hefflefinger. He reports the discovery to Michael E. Dwyer and insists on accompanying him and Hefflefinger to the planned arrest.

l: the Press, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The Press employs Gallegher as an office-boy, though its managing editor discharges him after repeated truancy. Michael E. Dwyer plans to seek his reinstatement after Gallegher's discovery of Hade.

l: Philadelphia, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Philadelphia is where Gallegher lives and works and where he has detailed knowledge of police districts, criminals, and transportation. The city is also near Torresdale and the Eagle Inn, where Hade is believed to be hiding.

l: Richard F. Burrbank, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Richard F. Burrbank was a prominent New York railroad lawyer and wealthy railroad-stock owner. He was found dead at the foot of his hall stairs with two pistol wounds above his heart.

l: the Burrbank murder, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The Burrbank murder is one of the two major news stories occupying the newspapers. It concerns Richard F. Burrbank's killing, the opening of his safe, the theft of $200,000, and the disappearance of his secretary, Stephen S. Hade.

l: Hade, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Stephen S. Hade was Richard F. Burrbank's secretary and is regarded as the murderer based on circumstantial evidence. He disappeared after Burrbank's death and the theft from the safe, and Gallegher believes he has found Hade hiding near Torresdale under the name Mr. Carleton.

l: the Champion of the United States, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The Champion of the United States is scheduled to take part in a major fight near Philadelphia.

l: the Would-be Champion, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The Would-be Champion is scheduled to fight the Champion of the United States near Philadelphia.

l: the Heenan-Sayers fight, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The big fight is a heavily publicized contest between the Champion of the United States and the Would-be Champion. It is scheduled to take place in the barn at the Eagle Inn, with tickets costing $250, and Hade may attend it to avoid suspicion.

l: Detective Hefflefinger, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Detective Hefflefinger, a member of Inspector Byrnes's staff, comes to Philadelphia seeking a burglar but finds that the burglar has escaped. Gallegher telegraphs him that Hade is near Torresdale and plans for him to make the arrest quietly using the warrant he already carries.

l: Inspector Byrnes, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Inspector Byrnes supervises the detective staff to which Detective Hefflefinger belongs.

l: New York, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: New York is the location of Richard F. Burrbank's murder and the destination for Hade after the planned arrest. Hade's description has been telegraphed and cabled worldwide, and the investigation concerns authorities there.

l: Kensington railroad station, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Kensington railroad station is near Gallegher's home and has trains running toward the suburbs and New York. Gallegher sees the suspected Hade there, follows him, and boards the train to Torresdale.

l: Torresdale, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Torresdale is a station outside Philadelphia where the suspected Hade gets off and walks toward the Eagle Inn. Gallegher telegraphs Detective Hefflefinger to meet him there, and plans call for Hade to be taken from the area on the one o'clock train.

l: the old Eagle Inn, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The Eagle Inn is an old roadside hostelry near Torresdale known as a gathering place for pothunters and cock-fights. The suspected Hade, using the name Mr. Carleton, is staying there, and the big fight is scheduled in its barn.

l: Mr. Carleton, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Mr. Carleton is the name used by the well-dressed, gloved man staying at the Eagle Inn. He claims to be in the country for his health, behaves nervously when asked about the fight, and is believed by Gallegher to be Stephen S. Hade.

l: Michael E. Dwyer, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: Michael E. Dwyer is the sporting editor who hears Gallegher's report and recognizes its importance. He plans to accompany Detective Hefflefinger, arrange a quiet arrest, keep the news from competing papers, and recommend Gallegher's reinstatement to the Press.

l: the $5,000 reward, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The $5,000 reward is offered for locating and delivering Hade to the police. Michael E. Dwyer tells Gallegher that the reward will belong to him if Hade is caught.

l: the stolen fortune, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The stolen fortune consists of $200,000 in bonds, stocks, and money taken from Richard F. Burrbank's safe. The property had been placed in the safe only the night before the murder.

l: Hade's arrest, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The arrest of Hade has not yet occurred in this unit. Gallegher and Michael E. Dwyer arrange for Detective Hefflefinger to arrest the suspected Hade quietly near the Eagle Inn and take him to New York on the one o'clock train.

l: the Burrbank murder investigation, Gallegher and Other Stories, RAEGEN THE OTHER WOMAN THE TRAILER FOR ROOM NO.
s: The investigation has produced a worldwide search for Stephen S. Hade, whose description was circulated by telegraph and cable. People suspected of being Hade have been arrested in various places, but Gallegher's discovery near Torresdale offers a possible breakthrough.

l: Gallegher and Other Stories, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: Gallegher and the sporting editor travel by cab to Torresdale to arrange Hade’s secret arrest during an illegal prizefight. At Keppler’s barn, Gallegher and Hefflefinger enter through a window and watch the fighters from a haymow while Dwyer identifies Hade in the crowd. When the police raid the barn, Hefflefinger seizes Hade and presents him as the burglar “Arlie” Lane, alias Carleton, so he can remove him secretly. Hade offers money for his release, but Hefflefinger refuses and takes him toward the train station.

l: Gallegher, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: Gallegher travels with the sporting editor and gives the cab driver directions to Torresdale. He arranges for the cab to have a clear escape route, enters Keppler’s barn through a window with Hefflefinger, watches the fight from a haymow, and helps identify and secure Hade. He praises Hefflefinger’s handling of the arrest and is told not to forget his share of the payment.

l: Michael E. Dwyer, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: The sporting editor travels with Gallegher to Torresdale, sends a message to the Press office, and sleeps during much of the cab ride. He negotiates with Hefflefinger for Hade’s secret arrest and promises a share of the reward.

l: Mr. Dwyer, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: Mr. Dwyer identifies himself as being from the Press and offers Hefflefinger $500 to arrest Hade secretly as though he were the burglar sought by the authorities. He enters Keppler’s barn, stays near Hade during the fight, and signals or identifies him for Hefflefinger.

l: Hade, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: Hade attends the fight in disguise, anxious because he fears Keppler and the danger of remaining away. During the police raid, Hefflefinger seizes him and threatens to reveal his real identity, while Hade offers money and a share of his fortune in exchange for release. He is identified as the murderer and is taken under the supposed name of the burglar “Arlie” Lane, alias Carleton.

l: Detective Hefflefinger, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: Hefflefinger agrees to arrest Hade secretly while pretending to arrest him for burglary. He enters the barn through a window, watches Hade throughout the fight, and captures him during the police raid. He refuses Hade’s bribe and says he will take him to the station and then to New York.

l: the Press, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: The Press receives a message from the sporting editor, and Mr. Dwyer identifies himself as its representative. The proposed payment depends on no other paper learning of Hade’s arrest.

l: the police, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: The police raid Keppler’s barn during the fight, breaking down the doors and causing a panic among the spectators. The officers allow Hefflefinger to pass after he displays his badge and explains that he is taking a burglar into custody.

l: the sporting crowd, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: The sporting crowd consists of sporting men, club-men, brokers, politicians, a comedian and his manager, amateur boxers, and others from cities around the country. Its members bet heavily, crowd around the ring, react violently to the fight, and panic when the police raid begins.

l: the fighters, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: The fighters enter the ring after the crowd has gathered and begin a brutal, closely contested bout. One fighter loses favor as the fight continues, while the other gains the advantage through repeated severe blows.

l: New York, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: New York is the destination of the train on which Dwyer and Hefflefinger plan to remove Hade. The reward arrangement also depends on no newspaper in New York or elsewhere learning of the arrest.

l: Torresdale, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: Torresdale is the destination of the cab journey and the location of the station near the old Eagle Inn. The fight takes place nearby at Keppler’s barn, where Hade is arrested.

l: the barn (Keppler's barn), Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: Keppler’s barn is a large building containing stalls, haymows, a ring, and a crowd gathered for an illegal fight. Gallegher and Hefflefinger enter through a window, and the police later raid it during the bout.

l: McGovern's cab, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: The cab carries the sporting editor and Gallegher through a cold, snowy, partly rural journey to Torresdale. It is later positioned near the lower gate with its lamps extinguished so the newspaper men can make a rapid departure.

l: the train, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th
s: The train passing the Torresdale station at 1.20 is intended to carry Hade secretly toward New York after his arrest. Hefflefinger plans to take that train with him.

l: Hade's arrest, Gallegher and Other Stories, " The sporting editor stepped into the waiting cab, while Gallegher whispered th

s: Miss Catherwaight's collection contains more than a hundred medals and decorations purchased during travels with her father. Each was awarded for public service, virtue, bravery, statesmanship, or artistic genius and was later pawned or sold by its recipient. She calls the collection dishonored honors, the Orders of the Knights of the Almighty Dollar, pledges to patriotism and the pawnshops, and honors at second-hand.

l: Lewis Lyman Lockwood, Gallegher and Other Stories, THE CYNICAL MISS CATHERWAIGHT Miss Catherwaight's collection of orders and decorations and medals was her chief offence in the eyes of those of her dear friends who thought her clever but cynical.
s: Lewis Lyman Lockwood is a lawyer whose office Miss Catherwaight visits after finding a medal bearing his name. Mr. Latimer says the medal had been in Lockwood's safe when he lived on Thirty-fifth Street and was taken by burglars. Lockwood had been devoted friends with Henry Burgoyne, but they quarrelled over a woman and have remained apart.

s: Judge Burgoyne is identified by Mr. Latimer as Henry Burgoyne, the former boyhood friend of Lewis Lockwood. He and Lockwood attended school together, roomed together at the State college, practised law together, and shared a love of shooting. He later became estranged from Lockwood after both men fell in love with the same woman.
